overview: Kogan.com is an Australian-founded (2006) e-commerce company operating a portfolio of retail and services businesses across Australia and New Zealand, anchored by the Kogan.com marketplace/retail platform and the Mighty Ape NZ online retailer (acquired December 2020). The Group sells Exclusive Brand and Third-Party Brand products often at thin or negative margin to acquire and retain customers, then monetises the resulting base through capital-light Platform-based Sales -- Marketplace seller fees, the Kogan FIRST/Mighty Ape PRIMATE subscription programs, commission-based Verticals (mobile, energy, insurance, credit card, travel), and Advertising. FY2026 revenue was $510.7 million across roughly 3.7 million group active customers (H1 FY2026).

business_model.summary: Two-pillar model: (1) Products division sells Exclusive Brands and Third-Party Brands at aggressive prices, often near or below cost, to acquire and retain a large customer base; (2) Platform-based Sales (Marketplace seller commissions, Kogan FIRST/PRIMATE subscriptions, Verticals commissions, Advertising) monetise that base with high, capital-light margins and no inventory risk. Platform-based Sales generated 61% of FY2026 group gross profit, up from 59% in FY2025, and management targets continued mix-shift toward this segment.

revenue_streams.name: Marketplace (seller commissions, incl. Mighty Ape Marketplace)
Loyalty subscriptions (Kogan FIRST + Mighty Ape PRIMATE)
Verticals (mobile, energy, insurance, credit card, travel)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market value-focused consumers in Australia and New Zealand; Marketplace side is B2B2C (thousands of third-party sellers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Australia (Kogan.com, ~83% of group revenue) with New Zealand via Mighty Ape (~17% of group revenue, reporting in NZD translated at AUD/NZD 0.8628 for FY26)

competitive_position.market_position: Kogan is now the only remaining dedicated Australian-owned online marketplace of scale after the closures of Catch.com.au and MyDeal, but its share of Australian shopper usage has been declining (cited at ~15%, down ~6pp YoY in a 2026 industry report) as Amazon (reaching ~60% of shoppers), Temu (A$2.6bn sales, 47% reach) and Shein (30% reach, fastest-growing) collectively push toward a third of Australian online retail sales.

moat_factors.description: ~19 years of Exclusive Brand development (Kogan, Ovela, Fortis, Ergolux, Komodo) and ~3.7m active group customers provide a recognisable, trusted local alternative to offshore marketplaces, with faster local delivery than Temu/Shein
Kogan FIRST ($57.0m FY26 revenue, up 11%) and Mighty Ape PRIMATE create recurring revenue and higher engagement/repeat purchase; deferred income growing (+17.6% to $10.4m)
Low-capital commission model piggybacking on partners (TPG, One NZ, NAB, Shell Energy) diversifies revenue away from pure retail margin, but is not defensible IP -- partners could disintermediate
Lean headcount, in-house tech platform and recent AI deployment (customer care automation from March 2026) support scaling revenue without proportionate cost growth
Positioned as a value/discount retailer, but Temu and Shein now undercut Kogan on price for many categories, eroding the traditional 'unbeatable value' differentiator

weaknesses: No structural network effect or switching cost comparable to Amazon Prime's ecosystem or Temu/Shein's scale-driven cost base
Thin/negative product-division margins mean the Products pillar is a customer-acquisition loss-leader dependent on Platform-based Sales to generate group profit
Mighty Ape suffered a severe operational and reputational setback (platform migration failure, $46.3m goodwill write-off, FY25 restated equity) that took over two years to stabilise
Reliance on third-party commercial partners (TPG, One NZ, NAB, Shell Energy) for most Verticals revenue -- limited control over service quality or partner terms
Small balance sheet net asset base ($34.4m equity FY2026) leaves little buffer against a further shock

growth_drivers: Continued Platform-based Sales mix-shift (Marketplace, Loyalty, Verticals, Advertising) toward the targeted 50-55% adjusted margin range, expanding group Adjusted EBITDA margin toward the medium-term 8-12% target and longer-term aspiration of >20%

Mighty Ape turnaround completing -- returned to positive quarterly Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY26 after a two-year reset (site migration remediation, inventory clearance, cost base reduction), with PRIMATE, Mighty Ape Marketplace and Mighty Mobile all scaling rapidly off a low base
Kogan FIRST/PRIMATE subscriber growth and Marketplace seller expansion, both capital-light and high incremental margin
AI deployment across customer care (from March 2026) and internal product/engineering/operations processes to cut serving costs and enable headcount-light scaling
Kogan Products division Gross Profit growth outpacing revenue growth (FY26: GP +33.4% vs revenue +18.0%) on improved sourcing, supplier negotiation and mix
New Kogan Trading US Inc subsidiary established in FY26 (no activity yet) -- potential optionality for US market entry

Ongoing capital return via buybacks (10% of issued capital authorised April 2026, ~5.2% completed by 30 June 2026) and fully franked dividends signal management confidence and support EPS/DPS per-share metrics even as revenue growth is moderate

business.description: Amazon, Temu and Shein are capturing rising shopper reach and an estimated one-third of Australian online retail sales in 2026, while Kogan's own usage share has fallen; Kogan is now the last major local marketplace standing after Catch and MyDeal shut down, underscoring the structural pressure on the model

The FY25 website migration failure caused a severe revenue and profit collapse and a $46.3m goodwill impairment; although Q4 FY26 showed a return to positive Adjusted EBITDA, the turnaround is described by management as 'at an early stage' and full-year segment profitability is not yet proven
Products division still trades near breakeven; competitive/price pressure could force further margin compression, especially from Temu/Shein's direct-from-factory cost base
Kogan Mobile/Internet (TPG), Kogan Energy (Shell), Kogan Money (NAB), Mighty Mobile (One NZ) revenue depends on continued favourable commercial partnerships that Kogan does not control

business.risk: Customer concentration in a narrow value segment
business.description: Heavy reliance on price-sensitive, deal-seeking consumers makes revenue sensitive to promotional cadence and discounting intensity from rivals

financial.risk: Thin equity base after restatement, impairment and capital returns
financial.description: Shareholders' equity fell from $60.5m (as originally reported FY25) to a restated $53.9m after an inventory-accrual review at Mighty Ape, and further to $34.4m by FY2026 year-end after $20.2m of buybacks and $13.0m of dividends net of DRP -- leaving a small net-asset cushion (NTA per share only $0.04 at 30 June 2026, down from $0.19 a year earlier)

The FY26 annual report restated the FY2025 balance sheet after reviewing Mighty Ape inventory-related accruals, indicating a historical control weakness in that subsidiary's finance function around the platform migration period
Mighty Ape results are translated from NZD (FY26 average rate AUD/NZD 0.8628); a weaker NZD reduces reported group revenue and profit from the NZ segment

No external bank debt since FY2022 and net cash of $36.4m at FY2026 year-end, but the Group carries $15-23m of lease liabilities (warehouse/fulfilment) that represent a fixed operating cost commitment
A $21.1m deferred tax asset write-down depressed FY2024 net income to near zero, illustrating how non-cash tax items can swing headline profit independent of underlying trading

regulatory.risk: Consumer protection / ACCC scrutiny of discount and 'was/now' pricing claims
regulatory.description: Value-retailers using large headline discounts face ongoing ACCC attention to pricing representations; historical Kogan Mobile/ACCC issues (unrelated to marketplace) illustrate regulatory sensitivity in the sector

Kogan Money Credit Card, Kogan Insurance and Kogan Energy operate under partner AFSL/energy retail licences; changes to consumer credit, insurance distribution or energy retail regulation in Australia/NZ could affect commission economics

Any tightening of GST/customs enforcement on low-value imported parcels (the type Temu/Shein rely on) could relatively benefit Kogan, but the reverse (further loosening or non-enforcement) sustains the current competitive disadvantage

macro.description: Cost-of-living pressure and softer consumer confidence in New Zealand were explicitly cited as compounding Mighty Ape's FY25 downturn; group revenue and margins are correlated with discretionary retail conditions
Low direct exposure given net cash position and no bank debt, but higher-for-longer rates dampen discretionary consumer spending indirectly

macro.risk: Freight, FX and global sourcing costs
macro.description: Products division sources internationally (own-brand manufacturing plus Third-Party Brands); shipping costs, tariffs and AUD/USD movements affect landed cost of goods

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian e-commerce continues to grow, but the competitive structure is consolidating around global-scale players (Amazon, Temu, Shein) at the expense of local marketplaces; industry commentary in 2026 forecasts these three offshore players alone could generate over $18bn in Australian sales and capture more than a third of online retail
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high -- discretionary consumer electronics/homewares spending is sensitive to consumer confidence and household budgets in both Australia and New Zealand
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct balance-sheet sensitivity (net cash, no bank debt) but moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending
key_input_costs: Supplier/sourcing costs for Exclusive Brand products

recent_developments.event: FY2026 results released: group revenue $510.7m (+4.6%), statutory NPAT $11.2m (vs FY25 loss of $39.5m), Adjusted NPAT $19.4m, gross sales surpassed $1bn for the first time; shares fell ~15% on the day despite the improvement, as investors focused on group-level growth deceleration (constituent Kogan.com grew revenue 16% but Mighty Ape revenue fell ~30%) and execution risk on FY27 targets

Board declared a fully franked final dividend of 8.0 cents/share (record date 11 Sept 2026, paid 30 Nov 2026), taking FY26 total dividends to 16.0 cents/share, up from 14.0 cents in FY25; DRP applies at 2.5% discount
Board approved a new on-market buyback for up to 10% of issued capital (9,548,224 shares), running to May 2027; 5.16m shares (~5.2%) repurchased for $20.2m by 30 June 2026

AI deployed across Kogan.com Customer Care operations, automating a significant share of enquiries and reducing servicing costs, part of a broader internal AI rollout across product/engineering/operations

H1 FY2026 results: revenue $287.6m (+5.5%), Kogan.com segment revenue +16.9%, Mighty Ape revenue -25.3% (deliberate inventory clearance); group active customers reached 3.7m (+22.9% YoY); statutory NPAT $8.2m; cash $71.8m, no debt
Mighty Ape generated its first positive quarterly Adjusted EBITDA ($0.4m) since the FY25 platform-migration crisis, aided by a reprofiled cost base and PRIMATE/Marketplace/Mighty Mobile growth

FY2025 results: statutory net loss of $39.5m after a $46.3m non-cash goodwill impairment on Mighty Ape, following the failed website migration and NZ consumer weakness; board changes announced with three new independent non-executive directors (Francine Ereira, Gary Levin, Ronn Bechler) appointed August 2025, and James Spenceley resigned September 2025
FY2025 comparative balance sheet restated after a review of inventory-related accruals at Mighty Ape, reducing previously reported FY25 shareholders' equity from $60.5m to $53.9m
Founder/CEO Ruslan Kogan purchased ~1m shares on-market at ~A$4.77/share (a ~6.3% increase to his direct holding), signalling insider confidence

items.target: medium-term goal of progressively growing toward 12%
items.notes: Reiterates the FY25 medium-term range of 8-12% Adjusted EBITDA margin, moving toward the top end; longer-term aspiration remains >20%, unchanged from FY25 commentary
Consistent with FY25 guidance; Platform-based Sales share of gross profit rose to 61% in FY26 from 59% in FY25

items.target: return to full-year Adjusted EBITDA profitability
items.vs_prior: raised (from 'H2 FY26 recovery' to explicit full-year target)
items.notes: Q4 FY26 delivered the first positive quarterly Adjusted EBITDA ($0.4m); management guiding to sustained full-year profitability in FY27
Continues FY25 commentary; FY26 Kogan Products gross margin expanded 2.4pp to 21.1%

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasised the milestone of exceeding $1 billion in Group Gross Sales for the first time, continued Kogan.com growth across Products, Marketplace, Advertising and Verticals, a shift toward higher-margin Platform-based Sales requiring less working capital, and AI-driven efficiency gains. Despite the positive tone, the market reaction (shares down ~15% on results day) reflected skepticism about the sustainability of margin expansion amid cost-of-living pressure, competitive dynamics in Australian e-commerce/marketplaces, marketing spend efficiency, and the early-stage nature of the Mighty Ape recovery.

bull_case: Platform-based Sales (Marketplace, Loyalty, Verticals, Advertising) now generate 61% of group gross profit and are scaling with high incremental margins and minimal capital intensity, providing a credible path to the medium-term 8-12% (and longer-term >20%) Adjusted EBITDA margin target

Mighty Ape turnaround is inflecting -- first positive quarterly Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY26 after a two-year reset -- removing a major earnings drag and offering a re-rating catalyst if full-year profitability is achieved in FY27

Kogan is the last major Australian-owned online marketplace standing after Catch and MyDeal closures, retaining brand recognition, local logistics speed and ~3.7m active customers versus a field of offshore-only competitors

Net cash balance sheet (no bank debt) with continued cash generation ($38.3m FY26 FCF, +18.2% YoY) funds an active capital return program (buybacks plus a growing fully franked dividend, 16.0 cents/share in FY26) even amid a thin equity base
Insider buying by founder/CEO Ruslan Kogan and AI-driven cost efficiencies (customer care automation from March 2026) support management alignment and further operating leverage
bear_case: Structural competitive threat from Amazon, Temu and Shein is intensifying -- collectively approaching a third of Australian online retail sales in 2026 -- while Kogan's own marketplace usage share has been declining, raising doubt about the long-term durability of the local marketplace model

Shareholders' equity has been eroded sharply: from $60.5m (as originally reported) to a restated $53.9m at FY2025 year-end, and further to just $34.4m by FY2026 year-end after continued buybacks and dividends, leaving little balance-sheet buffer (NTA/share only $0.04) against a future shock

Mighty Ape's FY25 platform-migration failure, $46.3m goodwill impairment and subsequent FY25 accrual restatement raise questions about financial and operational controls at the NZ subsidiary; the turnaround remains unproven on a full-year basis

Group-level growth is muted once Mighty Ape's deliberate revenue contraction is included (FY26 group revenue +4.6% vs Kogan.com standalone +16.2%), and the ~15% share-price fall on FY26 results day suggests the market is pricing in execution risk on FY27 margin and Mighty Ape targets

Core Products division still operates near breakeven margin and depends on continuing to out-price or out-service well-capitalised global rivals, while several Verticals revenue streams depend on third-party commercial partners (TPG, One NZ, NAB, Shell) that Kogan does not control
